chapter: Bucking contests, boogie woogie and rhythm
title: Bucking contests between bands, and the Roger Wolfe band
summary: Bands meeting on wagons would try to outdo each other with no declared winner; he likens it to a band he assembled against Roger Wolfe.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: The little magazine they put out. Yeah. Yeah, let me see. I wanted to get back to some more things, like, how do you decide who wins a bucking contest?
Oh, the bucking contest. Oh, well, well, well, that's all, all in that story. You didn't get a chance to read that thing about Smokey Mary.
I did, but I don't know how you decide who wins.
What do you mean? Who, who, who wins, who wins the contest? Who comes out on top? Well, I mean, uh, who knows?

They don't, they don't say, well, you win, I'll, I'll, you know. They don't, uh, that's, that, that was a natural thing with, and the bands that used to, used to, the same thing used to happen, like, uh, Kid Punch and, and, uh, and, uh, Sam Morgan. They used to go around advertising watermelons and stuff on these, on these, uh, carts, you know. They'd be in one of these wagons.

And they'd be playing on all the corners and stuff like that. And then sometimes two bands would meet on the corner somewhere, and they'd have a bucking contest right there. You know, just out, out, trying to outdo each other.

That, that's the whole deal. I mean, there's nobody, nobody says, well, you win and I, I lost and so forth. But, but, I mean, just everybody, they, they just felt, uh, well, we cut him a brand new one, you know. Just like, just like I was telling you about, uh, Roger, what's his name, uh, I showed you the picture that we did this Treasury broadcast.

Roger Wolfe. He had me, had me get a band together with Santo, and I told you the, the, the name of the guys, you know. And, and, and Papa Sillis there, see. So, that was a, sort of a bucking contest there, as far as I was concerned, you know.

I mean, I, I just wanted to cut him a brand new one and, and play that thing. And we had, had a wonderful band. And we just got him so mixed up that he got all mixed up on the thing. I, I got a tape on the thing.
And it was, it was all mixed up.
